verdicts.why: THE FALSE PASS IS REAL AND MEASURED — a stale `// const EXPECTED_TOTAL = 43;` above a live line the regex cannot read makes the test print GREEN off the comment (see experiment, mutF). The test's own stated contract at :70, 'read the runner's constant rather than trusting a copy', is defeated. TWO CORRECTIONS. (1) SEVERITY IS OVERSTATED. 'the live value can be anything' is only true of the RUNNER's constant. The consequence the test exists to prevent — a silently shrinking chaos gate — is still independently pinned from the other side by chaosGate.test.ts:66-68, `expect(ALL).toHaveLength(43)`, which counts plants by static import and trusts neither constant. And the brief's own doneCriterion mutation (lowering the live literal to 40 while the comment says 43) is caught LOUDLY by the runner itself at chaos.ts:165 `if (!filtered && all.length !== EXPECTED_TOTAL)` → 'PLANT COUNT DRIFTED: found 43, expected 40', fatal. So the exploitable window is narrow: the live line must become a form the regex cannot parse (a computed or env-driven expression), which is also the only form that makes chaos.ts:165 vacuous. That is real and it is the case I proved, but it is not 'the guard silently stops guarding' across the board. (2) THE PROPOSED FIX IS INSUFFICIENT, MEASURED: `/^const EXPECTED_TOTAL = (\d+);$/m` still reads 43 out of a block comment whose inner line starts at column 0 (mutD below) — ^ anchors to a LINE start, and a /* ... */ line is at a line start. The fix must strip comments first (JClaw's own withoutComments, the very lesson this candidate cites) or assert exactly one match of the identifier in assignment position, which the brief's second clause hints at but its regex does not do.

Then ran a node script (probe.mjs / probe2.mjs) applying tests/chaosGate.test.ts:73's regex VERBATIM, `/const EXPECTED_TOTAL = (\d+);/.exec(src)?.[1]`, plus the brief's proposed `/^const EXPECTED_TOTAL = (\d+);$/m`, and reporting whether `expect(found).toBe('43')` would pass. Mutations: orig = unchanged; A = `// const EXPECTED_TOTAL = 43;` above a live `= ALL_PLANTS.length`; B = same stale comment above a live `= 40`; C = constant RENAMED to PLANT_TOTAL (fail-closed probe); D = the same value inside a /* */ block whose inner line starts at column 0 (probes the PROPOSED fix); E = live line replaced by the realistic, legal, compiling `const EXPECTED_TOTAL = Number(process.env.CHAOS_TOTAL ?? 43);` with NO comment; F = E WITH the stale comment above it. E/F are the realistic exploit: A's `ALL_PLANTS.length` would not actually typecheck at chaos.ts:81 (the plant list is built later in the file), whereas an env-read compiles and turns the runner's own drift check at chaos.ts:165 into an off switch.
